title: Extreme Signal Efficiency and Ultrafast Detectors Powered by Pixelated Sensor Technology Designed for EBSD
content: Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) has become an indispensable technique for microstructural analysis within a Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM). Its widespread adoption across various fields, ranging from academic materials research to industrial applications in advanced materials development and failure analysis, is largely driven by two critical parameters: speed and signal efficiency. Since the introduction of the first automated EBSD systems in the 1990s, which were based on pioneering research by [1,2], the technique has seen remarkable advancements. Over the past three decades, continuous improvements in both hardware and software have significantly enhanced the speed and signal efficiency of EBSD systems. These advancements have not only increased the throughput of microstructural analysis but also improved the accuracy and resolution of the data obtained, making EBSD an essential tool for modern materials science and engineering.
